why: Inserting the ordering after C5 caused the model to prefer cutting after short (≤6-word) clausal/complement continuations instead of immediately before them, so many cuts shifted later. That change produced small net losses across all latency bins (by_bin all negative, larger harm for medium/long: ≤7 −0.0088, ≤99 −0.0106) with 1,947 worsened vs 1,790 improved — improvements are concentrated on very short/enumerative pieces while harm occurs when the later cut lands inside or after the following clause (e.g. moves cutting away from 'such as vomiting ‖ are sufficiently general' to a later split inside the predicate).
lesson: Respect that preferring to attach short clausal/complement continuations systematically shifts cuts later and, although it helps some very short/enumerative cases, it degrades medium/long segmentation so it should not be applied unconditionally.
